abstentions.record_text:
Hey everyone, 21+3 weeks and have an anterior placenta. I started feeling butterflies around 16 weeks like once every couple of days, and around week 20 I started feeling a kick or movement like once a night. Now, I can feel movement randomly but I usually need to be sitting or laying in bed and aware to feel it. 



I just got a belly band because my work is physical labor and I started getting lower back/hip pain. I've only worn it 2 days, but its definitely helping me feel more when I'm walking, working, or not actively trying to feel movement. I haven't heard anyone else talk about this. I'm not sure if it could help anyone else, but I think they are worth a try!

abstentions.record_text:
I am 26 weeks and still running 3 miles twice a week. Around week 22 my belly started feeling heavy and my regular compression tights were cutting it.

I pulled out a pair of Lasora leggings I bought back in my first trimester. I had only worn them to work but the belly band is pretty substantial so I figured I would test them on a run. Four runs in and the band stays put. The leg compression is solid. I did a 5k last weekend and they never rolled down.

But by mile 2 I still wanted more lift. I grabbed a cheap belly band for my next run and the combo felt way better. The leggings are great on their own for shorter stuff and the gym. For longer runs in the third trimester I think you need both.

Has anyone else run in them? Did the support last you through the whole pregnancy or did you end up adding a belt?

abstentions.record_text:
This is my third pregnancy. While I was lucky to be able to exercise (walking and weights mostly) through my first two, I had to give up running very early due to pelvic pain. 

Not sure what’s going on this time, but I’m currently 29 weeks pregnant and still running 3-4 miles 3 days a week (really … more of a light trot at this point ha). I’ve set the goal of doing as many 5Ks as I can for as long as I can, and not worrying about pace, which has helped stay within reasonable goals. I also think having a treadmill now (downhills outside are a little uncomfy) and actually using a belly band are helping. But it mostly seems to be just another way every pregnancy is so different. 

I’m taking it a week at a time, but curious if anyone has been able to continue running/jogging up to your due date? And any tips to do it safely/not destroy your pelvic floor? Should I be using anything other than a belly band?

c13_check.reason: n_records=32 >= 8, n_authors=31 >= 2, agreement=81.2% >= 70%, single_coded=True; the Directional threshold still passes
c13_check.claims_evidence_gap_check: no claim becomes Evidence gap because of the confidence gate; C03 remains Evidence gap for its pre-existing structural reason (0 exact-model first-person experience records)

build_level_sensitivity.definition: high confidence AND polarity not in {unknown, mixed}; this is what llm_coder.code_record actually emits as annotations
build_level_sensitivity.why: one high-confidence gold-set aspect (c-1s8bn5y, SUP.GENERAL, gold polarity also unknown) is converted to an abstention by llm_coder.py:285-299; eval_gold.py by-confidence counting keeps it

comparability_with_ref_g7.ref_requirement: G7 requires a second independent coder and field-level agreement/kappa: ref/extract/DATA-CONTRACT.md:736 lists agreement, second_coder_id, field_level_kappa; voc-research-charter.json sets semantic_core_cohen_kappa_min=0.8, identity_governance_cohen_kappa_min=0.9, risk_case_review_coverage=1.0.
why_87_is_not_080: precision is TP/(TP+FP) for one coder against a reference; it ignores false negatives. High-only strict recall is 47.1%, so 45 of 85 gold aspects are missed.
agreement/kappa is symmetric between two coders and Cohen kappa removes chance agreement. A raw precision of 87.0% is not 0.87 kappa.
the strict F1 is 61.1% and Jaccard is 44.0% (illustrative symmetric overlap, not kappa); both are far below 0.80.

the gold set is a single reference annotation. voc/report.py:29-31 and 515 describe it as an LLM annotation; gold-set-50.jsonl records no second_coder_id. The 87.0% is therefore at best inter-LLM precision, not human double-blind agreement.
the sample is 50 records / 85 gold aspects; Reddit has 8 gold aspects. One Reddit FP moves precision by 12.5-25 pp, so the estimate cannot establish a 0.80 threshold.
missing: a second independent coder (second_coder_id) and a blind coding protocol
human-verified gold or human adjudication of disagreements
a pre-registered field-level Cohen kappa, not raw precision/agreement
a pre-registered abstention rule: high-only abstains on 18/64 gold-set coder aspects (28.1%); G7 must say whether abstentions are missing data or disagreement
the full G7 sample design: ref has core 50 + boundary 6 + frame eligibility 2 = 58 distinct records; this gold set is 50 records with no boundary/frame-eligibility strata
the other G7 thresholds: identity/governance kappa >= 0.9 and risk case review coverage = 1.0

structural_ceiling: gold contains 2 qualified_positive aspects; the coding contract forbids emitting qualified_positive, so strict recall can never reach 100% on those units.
two gold records exceed the contract 6-aspect cap (14 and 8 aspects); recall on those records is structurally truncated regardless of confidence.
notes: gold set is unchanged; gold denominators stay at 85 for ALL, 77 for TikTok, 8 for Reddit.
high-only filters LLM aspects, not records: no record is dropped wholesale.
family and code-only coincide on this gold set because every code-only match also agrees on polarity family.
the high-only point estimate is below 90 but the 95% Wilson interval (74.3-93.9) still contains 90; the sample cannot resolve a 90% threshold with confidence.
